title: Shadows and Reflection
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Shadows and Reflection Worksheets (Shadow Size, Mirrors, Periscopes)
standard_text: Use the idea that light travels in straight lines to explain why shadows have the same shape as the objects that cast them.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on shadows and reflection: why shadows have the same shape as objects, shadow size investigations, shadows from the Sun, mirrors and periscopes. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Closer to the light, bigger shadow; mirrors reflect at equal angles.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light travels in straight lines, so opaque objects make shadows with the same outline.

  • Move an object closer to the light and its shadow gets bigger; move it away and the shadow gets smaller.
  • Outdoors, shadows are long in the morning and evening and shortest at midday. They point away from the Sun.
  • Mirrors reflect light: the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. A periscope uses two mirrors at 45°.
Example

Shadow 50 cm at 10 cm, 20 cm at 40 cm. At 25 cm?

Between the 20 cm and 30 cm results

Answer: between those heights

Example

Ray hits a mirror at 35°. Reflected angle?

Angle in = angle out

Answer: 35°

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a shadow is a reflection.
  • Thinking moving the object away from the light makes the shadow bigger.
  • Thinking shadows are longest at midday.

faq.q: Why do shadows have the same shape as the object?
faq.a: Light travels in straight lines. An opaque object blocks the light, so the dark area behind it has the same outline as the object.

faq.q: How can you change the size of a shadow?
faq.a: Move the object closer to the light to make the shadow bigger, or further from the light (closer to the screen) to make it smaller.
It has two mirrors at 45°. Light reflects off the top mirror down the tube, then off the bottom mirror into your eye.
